title: Portfolio projects file
description: Validates projects.json. Most code editors read the $schema link at the top of projects.json and will underline mistakes (missing fields, wrong types, typo'd field names) as you type. This file is documentation + editor tooling only; the loader in projects.js does its own lightweight runtime check.

$schema.description: Points at this schema file so editors validate the data.

projects.description: One object per project. Add a project by copying an existing object and editing it.

name.description: Project title, shown as-is. The URL-style slug (used by the terminal's `cat projects/NAME`) is derived from this automatically.

languages.description: Programming / markup / styling languages (e.g. TypeScript, Python, CSS). Can be empty. Becomes a 'Languages' filter facet.

tools.description: Frameworks, libraries, services, platforms, and APIs (e.g. React, Firebase, Docker, Canvas API). Becomes a 'Tools' filter facet.

skills.description: What this project demonstrates. Free-form labels — no fixed list. Becomes a 'Skills' filter facet and is also searchable text.

github.description: Repository URL, or null if the repo is private / has no public link. The card simply omits the GitHub link when this is null.

website.description: Live site / demo URL, or null to hide the link.

summary.description: One or two sentences. Always visible on the card.

description.description: Detailed description. Each string is one paragraph. Shown when a card is expanded or the project is `cat`-ed in the terminal.

highlight.description: Which block leads on the collapsed card, so each project can foreground its most interesting part. 'skills' for a project built to learn something; 'description' for one where the story matters most. Omit or null to show just the basics.

started.description: YYYY or YYYY-MM, when the project began. Drives sort order (newest first). NOT shown to visitors. null keeps the project in file order, after dated ones.

lastWorked.description: YYYY or YYYY-MM, when you last worked on it. Metadata only — NOT shown to visitors and does not affect sort, so a bug-fix commit won't reorder your projects.

inProgress.description: true marks a project as not yet finished: the minimal card shows an 'In progress' chip, the terminal shows [wip], and both layouts can filter to only these. Omit it (or false) for finished projects. Does not affect sort order.
